note: Pure read. Re-issue is always safe. Result may differ if the world changed, but no effect is duplicated.
Whole-content write is naturally idempotent: f(f(x)) == f(x). Re-issue is safe by construction.

Re-issue rejected with "old_string not found". Content-addressed precondition means a replay either applies exactly once or fails loudly. Doubled=false. This is the strongest recovery property found and it requires NO idempotency key.
Re-issue duplicated the effect (2 lines, expected 1). Shell commands are opaque: the runtime cannot know whether "echo x >> f" is safe to repeat. THIS IS THE HARD CASE.
Same tool (bash), opposite safety. Proves safety is a property of the ARGUMENTS, not the tool.
Second commit refused (nothing to commit); history depth=1. Git refuses an empty commit, and state is verifiable via rev-parse. Recovery = compare HEAD to the recorded sha (b9a2a746).
Server saw 2 requests. Classic at-least-once hazard. Unrecoverable without a key or a server-side query to check whether the first one landed.
Deduped server-side: both calls returned id=1. Requires the REMOTE to honour the key — the harness cannot provide this property itself, only propagate it.
2 emails sent. Irreversible AND undetectable from the harness. Must escalate.
First=applied, second=already-applied, rows=1. When the effect and the dedup marker commit in ONE transaction, exactly-once is achievable. This is the only class with a real guarantee.
Creates a durable HumanRequest; re-issue is deduped by request_id. No external effect.
